entry.title: Gupta's 1967 conjecture on multigraph edge-coloring
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph, write $\mu(G)=\mu$, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. Assume that $\Delta(G)$ cannot be expressed as $2p\mu-q$ for integers satisfying $q\geq 0$ and $p>\lfloor(q+1)/2\rfloor$.

**Gupta's conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi'(G)\leq\Delta(G)+\mu(G)-1.
$$

The source states that this conjecture can be deduced from the Goldberg–Seymour conjecture, so it is solved in this paper's context.

entry.title: Tree-chromatic weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture
entry.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph and let $t$ be an integer. The **tree-chromatic number** $\mathsf{tree}\textnormal{-}\chi(G)$ is the minimum, over tree-decompositions of $G$, of the maximum chromatic number of a bag. **Tree-chromatic Hadwiger conjecture.** If $G$ is a graph without a $K_{t+1}$-minor, then $\mathsf{tree}\textnormal{-}\chi(G) \leqslant t$. This is proposed as a weakening of Hadwiger's conjecture and is open; the paper proves it for $t=5$ without using the Four Colour Theorem.
entry.source_name: Tony Huynh, Bruce Reed, David R. Wood and Liana Yepremyan, “Notes on Tree- and Path-chromatic Number”, arXiv:2002.05363 (2020).

entry.title: Finite generation of dual K-theory under graph deletion and contraction
entry.statement:
For a fixed $n$, let $UConf_n(\Gamma)$ be the unordered configuration space of $n$ points on a graph $\Gamma$, and consider the dual of its Grothendieck group of complex vector bundles as the functor

$$
\Gamma \longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}}(K^0(UConf_n(\Gamma)),\mathbb{Z}).
$$

Here $K^0$ denotes the Grothendieck group of vector bundles.

**Finite generation of dual K-theory.** For every fixed $n$, the dual of the Grothendieck group of vector bundles over configuration spaces of graphs

$$
\Gamma \longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb{Z}}(K^0(UConf_n(\Gamma)),\mathbb{Z})
$$

is generated by finitely many functions on vector bundles under deletion and contraction.

This proposes a finite-generation statement for dual K-theory in the setting where deletion and contraction induce maps between configuration spaces. The supplied source does not state whether the conjecture is open or has been resolved.
entry.assessment: Fixed-n minor functor: no integral K-theory finite generating set or natural deletion/contraction transport proved; rational homology finite generation would leave integral lattice/torsion and functoriality bridges.

entry.title: Alon–Tarsi bound for vertex-face graphs of plane graphs
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph, and let $G_{vf}$ denote its vertex-face graph. The **Alon–Tarsi conjecture.** Every plane graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{AT}(G_{vf})\leqslant 7.
$$

This would extend the corresponding list-colouring bound, whose optimality is unknown; the authors explain that proving non-vanishing of the relevant graph-polynomial monomial would establish the claim.
entry.finding_and_exact_unpaid_lemma: Conjecture1 AT(Gvf)<=7. Multiplying individually nonzero monomials does not prevent cancellation of their product coefficient. Need a nonzero coefficient with all exponents <=6 for every plane graph.

entry.title: Burr–Erdős linear Ramsey conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
entry.literal_statement: Let $\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$. A graph has **bounded maximum degree** at most $\Delta$ when $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. **Burr–Erdős conjecture.** There exists $c=c(\Delta)>0$ such that every $2$-edge-colored $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of every graph $G$ with at most $cn$ vertices and $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. This is a foundational linear Ramsey-number conjecture for sparse graphs; the supplied source does not indicate whether this formulation is resolved.

entry.title: Alon–Tarsi bound for combined vertex-edge-face graphs
entry.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph, and let $\overline{G}_{vef}$ denote its combined vertex-edge-face graph. The **Alon–Tarsi conjecture.** Every plane graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{AT}(\overline{G}_{vef})\leqslant 7.
$$

If true, this would improve the preceding Alon–Tarsi bound for $\overline{G}_{vef}$ and the known list-colouring bound $\operatorname{ch}(\overline{G}_{vef})\leqslant 8$; the source notes that the latter bound's tightness is unknown.

entry.literal_statement: Let $r\in\mathbb{N}$. An **$r$-colored** $K_{\mathbb{N},\mathbb{N}}$ is an assignment of one of $r$ edge colors to every edge of the infinite complete bipartite graph. **Partition conjecture.** The vertices of every $r$-colored $K_{\mathbb{N},\mathbb{N}}$ can be partitioned into a finite set and at most $r$ monochromatic paths. The source says that the analogous statement is believed for multiple colors, while the supplied text does not report a resolution.

entry.title: Jacobian-dual formulation of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture

literal.statement: Let $D$ be a digraph on $n$ vertices, let $G(D)$ be its associated bipartite graph, let $M_D$ be the perfect matching associated with $D$, and let $\phi$ be the Taylor presentation matrix of the edge ideal $I(G(D))$. Write $\overline{B(\phi)}$ for the reduced Jacobian dual, and $I_q(\overline{B(\phi)})$ for its ideal of $q\times q$ minors. **Jacobian-dual formulation of the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture.** If every vertex of $D$ has outdegree at least $\dfrac{n}{\ell}$, then for some $q\leq\ell$, the ideal $I_q(\overline{B(\phi)})$ contains a binomial with square-free, relatively prime terms, one of which is a product of elements of $M_D$. By the results established in the paper, this formulation is equivalent to the Caccetta-Häggkvist conjecture and translates directed-cycle existence into a condition on minors of a reduced Jacobian dual.
